reasons: Deviation is correctly identified: the original cap is limited to amounts 'ACTUALLY PAID ... FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO' with no USD floor, and the only carve-out is Section 8, so confidentiality/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and general indemnities all sit inside an illusory cap — below the walk-away/fallback threshold.

Redline reaches the preferred position: mutual cap reset to the greater of 12 months' fees 'paid or payable' by Corio and US$1,000,000, mutuality preserved ('either party'), a single Excluded Claims sentence added covering indemnification (including existing Section 8), confidentiality/data protection/security, gross negligence, willful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, plus the clarification that Corio's fee obligations are not capped damages.

Edit is surgical in structure — the existing two sentences and the 'reasonable allocation of risk' sentence are retained; the 0.744 changed-character ratio on the first operation is explained by the necessary replacement of the cap basis and the insertion of the carve-out definition, so the advisory failure does not indicate over-drafting.

Comment is accurate, correctly quotes the offending 'actually paid ... for the transaction' language, states the playbook position, notes indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap, and offers the straight 12-months'-fees fallback in the required tone.

Minor note (not disqualifying): substituting 'EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS' in the consequential-damages sentence broadens that exception beyond the model language on both sides; it mirrors the original drafting structure and is mutual, but the team should confirm it is acceptable that Corio could face consequential damages for carved-out breaches.
